finalText:
Build passes now (exit 0). You were right that it wasn't all noise — there were two actual bugs from the bump, hidden in ~950 lines of log:

1. **`src/core/options.js:6`** — the bundler renamed the option `retries` → `retryCount`, this call site still read `options.retries`, so it threw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toFixed')`. Now reads `retryCount`, falling back to `retries` for anything still on the old shape, with a clear TypeError if neither is a number.

2. **`src/net/retryPolicy.js:7`** — the old config loader returned `false` for unset flags; the new one leaves them `undefined`, which this strict check rejected. Unset now means off, matching the previous default. This one was sequential — it would only have surfaced after fixing #1.

On the remaining 8 warnings: those are genuinely non-blocking, but two look worth a follow-up ticket rather than leaving indefinitely:

- `W1042` — `crypto.createCipher` in `src/legacy/adapter.js`, flagged "remove before v5". That's an insecure API (no explicit IV) and a hard removal deadline.
- `W3307` — circular import between `src/core/graph.js` and `src/state/tracker.js` with undefined resolution order; that's the kind of thing that breaks unpredictably on the next bundler bump.

The rest (`DEP0142`, `DEP0198`, `DEP0233`, `DEP0250`, `DEP0267`, `W2213` unused export) are ordinary deprecation noise. I left all of them alone since the files aren't in this tree and you asked for a clean build, not a deprecation sweep — say the word if you want me to take on either of the two above.
